boundary: The result is an exact finite-module bridge. It does not identify the two 15-dimensional subspaces as literal coordinate subspaces: one uses the unsigned edge action and the other the orientation-signed edge action. The theorem is the natural equivariant intertwiner between those actions.

mod2_refinement: F mod 2 has rank 14 and square zero. Its kernel on the 45-dimensional modular cokernel has dimension 31, leaving a canonical 14-dimensional quotient. This selects the nontrivial 14 in the reduction of the rational 15; the second isomorphic 14 remains in the 31-dimensional kernel with factors 1,1,1,6,8,14.
theorem: Let M be the 540x240 canonical frame cross-matching matrix, N the unsigned point-edge incidence, d the oriented point-edge incidence, A the W33 adjacency matrix, and K the signed-turn operator. Then K d^T=d^T(6I-A). With P=(A-12I)(A-2I)=96E_{-4}, the integral matrix F=d^T P N/16 annihilates im(M^T), has rational rank 15, and has image ker(K-10I). Hence it induces an explicit PSp(4,3)-equivariant isomorphism coker(M) tensor Q -> ker(K-10I).
